# races

A playable race: picks, government, homeworld, AI personality tables, text keys and art. A new race borrows a stock race's starting relations through `relationsAs`.

A mod adds records in `records/races/<file>.json` (`{ "$schema": "carina-records/1", "catalog": "races", "records": [...] }`) and changes base records with patch rows on catalog `races`. Schema: [races records schema](../schemas/records/races.schema.json).

## Fields

A mod record leaves out `id` and `prov`: the game assigns ids, and `prov` is the project's own provenance.

## Also register it in

- [profile](patch-ops.md#special-catalogs) `availableRaces` (an `append` row on catalog `profile`, key `steam-dos-140b23`), so computer players can draw it at New Game
- `assets/roles.json` `races`: `{ "race": "<your race key>", "artBase": "<stock race key>" }`; every picture of the stock race stands in for one the mod does not bring

## Computer players

Computer players play a new race fully: its personality and objective weights are race data.

## Limits

- A mod race is on the paged Select Race screen (in the demo build under the custom-race terms: Small galaxy only).
- A new race needs its text keys in the mod's English text.
- Each race record carries `"$schema": "carina-race/1"` inside the `records` list of its records file.
- `roles` is optional and not used by the game; leave it out. The race's pictures come from `assets/roles.json`.
- Own pictures replace the art base's per role, at the same size: `races.portrait.select.<your race key>` and so on.
- Non-stock races have at most 10 pick points.
- A race either names an `artBase` (every role it leaves out is aliased to the base race's) or names none and then supplies the whole art contract (Hollow Choir does). A race with neither is refused `race-art-missing`, one issue listing every missing role.
- The contract is one role per family member of the stock races: the select, diplomacy and ambassador portraits, the select background, the two emblems, the council medallions, the ambassador scene, the research director, the six hulls of combat and picture atlases, `colony.pop`, the colonist figures, the spy and the trooper, plus `music.race.<your race key>` (Ogg and an m4a twin, at most 300 s). The other-sex portrait, ambassador and director (`-female`, or `-male` for a female-default race) are optional.
- Colonist figure atlases are 26x49 with frames `colony.<job>` (0,0,22,26) and `list.<job>` (0,27,26,22); the spy is a 17x23 image and the trooper 192x288.
- A mod race ships exactly one portrait per sex; the numbered variants (`.2` to `.4`) are the stock Humans' and are refused (`role-namespace`).
- In play a mod race's ships draw its own `shipsai.*` atlases and its audience plays `music.race.<your race key>` (a race with an art base plays the base race's theme).

- `set`: `$schema`, `aiPersonality`, `defaultRulerSex`, `flavourKey`, `government`, `homeStarKey`, `homeworld`, `homeworld.artifacts`, `homeworld.climate`, `homeworld.gravity`, `homeworld.minerals`, `homeworld.size`, `nameKey`, `picks`, `relationsAs`, `roles`, `roles.ambassadorPortrait`, `roles.ambassadorRoom`, `roles.emblem`, `roles.musicCue`, `roles.portrait`, `roles.selection`, `rulerNamesKey`, `singularKey`, `stock`, `variants`, `variants.hard`, `variants.impossible`
- `append`, `insertAfter`, `removeValue`: `aiPersonality`, `picks`, `variants.hard`, `variants.impossible`
